answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring every identity to stake slashable collateral and publish a unique work diary. When a gale of new accounts appears in one interval, the protocol compares each diary's stylistic quill—n-gram and timing fingerprints—against existing peers. Any cluster whose cosine similarity exceeds a published bound is quarantined, and a juniper-rooted Merkle of remaining honest attestations is what settles rewards, so cloned identities earn nothing.
